title.narrative: Protection, shelter/NFI, and CCCM support to vulnerable displaced populations in Yemen

description.narrative: This intervention will contribute to scaling-up multi-sectoral support for internally displaced persons (IDPs) and vulnerable host community members and households.UNHCR and partners will promote protection outcomes for vulnerable IDPs, returnees, and host community households through protection, shelter and NFI, and CCCM interventions. These interventions will strengthen capacities to exercise rights, to access essential services, to address basic needs, and ensure safer and more dignified living conditions, thus mitigating the need to resort to harmful coping mechanisms. Overall, a total of 11,435 households are expected to benefit from the project’s interventions which will include 2,000 instances of support to access civil documentation, 2,000 instances of legal assistance (including 1,000 instances using a cash modality), MPCA to 3,000 households, provision of 1,800 NFI kits, provision 1,700 emergency shelter kits (using a cash modality), provision of cash for maintenance of 1,200 shelters, and improvements to at least 7 IDP hosting sites benefitting at least 5,000 households (the final interventions will be defined based on the site assessments and based on the needs identified: interventions might, for example, include WASH interventions to improve access to water for the camp population). The interventions will target IDPs, returnees, and host community members identified as vulnerable and in need of assistance.Legal assistance and civil documentation are crucial in Yemen. Without documentation, vulnerable individuals are often unable to access basic rights and crucial, life-saving public services and humanitarian assistance. For example, documentation is required for IDPs to access WFP’s general food distribution programme. Legal assistance needed is often required in order to obtain civil documentation due to complications and missing pre-requisite documentation.
